title: When the Fitting ideal of a bounded complex with respect to a nonzerodivisor is principal, the shifted complex is locally free and its differential splits off
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The statement assumes that the Fitting ideal I_i(M, f) attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules and a nonzerodivisor is principal, and concludes that the shifted complex is locally free with explicit ranks and that its differential is the inclusion of a direct summand (statement lines 28049-28057). The proof works with the minors of the map (f, d^i): after localizing at f the rank is r_i, so the higher minors vanish, which makes the quotient by g-torsion finite locally free and f-torsion free, and the displayed complex of finite free modules is then used to identify the image of the second map with a projective module, after which the shifted term is recognised as a direct summand (proof lines 28059-28101). The subtle step is the passage from the cokernel to the cokernel modulo f-power torsion, which is what makes the projective module appear. The counted span refers twice, once to a fitting ideal statement of this chapter and once to the section in which the shifted complex is constructed, both carried as navigation stubs.
